story.title: Built for the clinics that need it most.
story.body:
Most hospital software is built for wealthy hospitals in stable economies. MediSina exists because the clinics that need it most — in Chad, Somalia, and beyond — deserve software that works for them, not against them.

Nonprofit. Built by clinicians and engineers. Funded by people who care.

clinic_day.title: Eight hours, one platform.
clinic_day.subtitle: Scroll to walk through a single clinic day with MediSina.
clinic_day.scene1_body: CoPilot Triage captures vitals from a Bluetooth thermometer, a photo, and three spoken questions. AI applies the Manchester Triage Scale, weighted for the local disease burden — malaria, dengue, cholera. The most urgent patient surfaces to position one.
clinic_day.scene2_title: Doctor speaks; the note structures itself.
clinic_day.scene2_body: Whisper Notes runs on-device in five languages. The clinician keeps eye contact with the patient. A structured SOAP note — chief complaint, history, exam, assessment, plan — appears in the record, ready for the doctor's signature.
clinic_day.scene3_body: A photo of the lab printout extracts structured values into the record. A photo of a microscope slide, taken through a five-dollar phone adapter, counts malaria parasites. AI is the second pair of eyes — never the last word.
clinic_day.scene4_body: Telegram, WhatsApp, and SMS reminders went out to 142 patients across five communities. Replies came back as structured updates the clinic team will act on at 08:00 tomorrow. The clinic closes — the platform keeps working.

deployment.title: Three ways to run MediSina.
deployment.subtitle: Same product, same audit trail, same data model. You pick the operating model that fits your clinic.

cloud.title: Cloud
cloud.body: Managed cloud (we operate it) or your own AWS, Azure, or GCP account (you operate it). Lowest setup, easiest to start; data residency stays in your jurisdiction when needed.

onprem.title: On-premise
onprem.body: Install on a server inside your clinic's local network. Patient data never leaves your walls. Works fully offline — sync is optional and configurable per-clinic.

mobile.title: Mobile
mobile.body: Progressive web app today — installable on any modern phone or tablet, works on flaky networks. Native iOS and Android apps on the 2026 roadmap.

product.subtitle: From patient intake to billing, every workflow lives in the same audit trail and the same role-based permission model.

for_hospitals.meta_description: Bring MediSina to your clinic. Deployment timeline, hardware requirements, funding paths, and FAQs.
for_hospitals.hero_title: Bring MediSina to your clinic in days, not months.
for_hospitals.hero_subtitle: Discovery, install, training, go-live — typically 4 to 6 weeks. We help match clinics with donor sponsors; for clinics that prefer to fund their own deployment, MediSina operates on a strict cost-recovery basis — no profit margin.

step1.title: Discovery call
step1.body: 30-minute conversation to understand your clinic's workflow, scale, and constraints — and whether you'd like sponsor matching or to fund deployment yourselves.

step2.title: Site assessment + sizing
step2.body: We size hardware, network, and training needs. Quoted as a tailored package — sponsor-funded or cost-recovery, your choice.

step3.title: Install + data setup
step3.body: On-site or remote, typically 1–2 days. Initial users, departments, master data loaded.

step4.title: Training + go-live
step4.body: One week of role-based workshops for clinicians, admin, and IT. Then live operations.

for_hospitals.need_1: A server (your own, ours, or a cloud account) plus a network
for_hospitals.need_2: Two or more client devices (any modern browser, phone, or tablet)
for_hospitals.need_3: An on-site staff member willing to be the in-clinic admin
for_hospitals.provide_2: Donor matching for clinics that need sponsorship
for_hospitals.provide_3: Ongoing software updates and security patches
for_hospitals.cost_title: Sponsor-funded, or strict cost-recovery — your choice.
for_hospitals.cost_body: MediSina is built and operated by a nonprofit. Many deployments are fully funded by donors and foundations who want to expand access to modern healthcare software. For clinics that prefer to operate independently — or aren't matched with a sponsor — MediSina works on a strict cost-recovery basis: we recover only what it costs to develop, install, and support, with no profit margin. Get in touch and we'll walk through both paths with you.

vision.meta_description: Five platform capabilities MediSina is building — AI triage, multilingual voice notes, diagnostic photo-in, WhatsApp/SMS patient channel, and a federated outbreak watch.
vision.hero_title: Beyond a record system. A clinical platform.
vision.hero_subtitle: Five capabilities that move the clinic from "data entry" to "data action" — built for the places where care happens despite the infrastructure.

f1.title: CoPilot Triage
f1.subtitle: From a 50-deep waiting room to a safe queue — in 30 seconds per patient.
f1.problem: Fifty patients waiting. Two nurses, one doctor. First-come, first-served is unsafe — the sickest patient might be the one stuck in hour two of the line.
f1.solution: A nurse walks the queue with a phone. A Bluetooth thermometer captures vitals, the camera captures one photo, and three spoken questions go to a small on-device model. AI applies the Manchester Triage Scale, weighted for the local disease burden — malaria, dengue, cholera. The waiting list reorders in real time, and the most urgent patient surfaces to the top within seconds, not hours.
f1.diff: Existing HBYS products require a manual triage form — minutes per patient, error-prone under load. We're building a voice + photo + AI triage flow that runs on the same phone the nurse already carries.

f2.title: Whisper Notes
f2.subtitle: Speak. We write. Five languages, on-device — no patient data leaves the clinic.
f2.problem: Clinicians lose half of every visit to typing. Eye contact is broken, examination is rushed, and notes stay shallow because there's simply no time to write more.
f2.solution: The clinician talks to the patient as they always have. The phone listens. Whisper.cpp on-device speech recognition plus a small local LLM transcribe and reshape the conversation into a structured SOAP note — chief complaint, history, examination, assessment, plan. The clinician reviews and signs. Works in Turkish, Arabic, Swahili, French, and English. No cloud round-trip, no PII leaving the building.
f2.diff: Nuance DAX and Suki cost $300 per clinician per month, run in the cloud, and ship English-only. We're building local-first, multilingual ambient documentation that runs on commodity hardware.

f3.title: Photo-In, Diagnosis-Out
f3.subtitle: Phone camera + AI = a portable laboratory and a second pair of eyes.
f3.problem: Lab printouts on paper. X-ray films held up to a window. Skin lesion referrals two hundred kilometres away. Microscope slides without an experienced microscopist on staff.
f3.solution: Snap a photo of a lab printout — OCR plus an LLM normaliser turn it into structured values in the patient record. Snap an X-ray — a CheXNet-derived screening model flags pneumonia risk and pleural effusion. Snap a skin lesion — a dermatology second-opinion model returns a benign/atypical score. Snap a microscope slide through a five-dollar phone adapter — a vision model counts parasites for malaria, TB, and helminths. Every AI output is the second pair of eyes, never the last word.
f3.diff: Google ARDA and AKi exist as separate services that don't connect to the patient record. We're folding four diagnostic AI assists into one clinical workflow — and all of them can run on-device when the clinic has no internet.

f4.title: Telegram, WhatsApp & SMS
f4.subtitle: Reach patients on the channels they already use. No app to install, ever.
f4.problem: Patient apps go uninstalled. Appointment reminders are phone calls one nurse makes between visits. Lab-ready notifications mean another bus ride to the clinic just to ask.
f4.solution: Telegram Bot API, WhatsApp Business API, and SMS fallback — the clinic picks the channel order per patient or per region. Automated, two-way: 24-hour appointment reminders that patients confirm with a single reply, lab-ready notifications carrying no PII over open channels, prescription pickup reminders, vaccine schedules, post-operative check-ins ("How is the pain on a scale of 0 to 10?"). Replies appear in the patient record as structured updates the clinician can act on.
f4.diff: Epic MyChart and Cerner HealtheLife require app downloads and run English-only by default. We're building patient communication on the channels patients are already on — Telegram, WhatsApp, or plain SMS — in the languages they already speak.

f5.title: Outbreak Watch
f5.subtitle: Your clinic, on the public-health radar. The federated sentinel network.
f5.problem: A single clinic alone can't see a regional outbreak — only national surveillance can, and by then a week or more has passed. Bridging that lag has historically required either expensive central systems or open data sharing that violates patient privacy.
f5.solution: Inside the clinic, Bayesian anomaly detection on diagnosis and symptom counts surfaces alerts in plain English — "watery diarrhea spike: +340% over baseline in the last 7 days." Across opt-in MediSina clinics in a region, federated learning shares privacy-preserving statistical signals — never patient data. WHO and national ministry of health reports are pre-formatted for one-click filing. A red badge appears on the admin dashboard days before the rest of the world knows.
f5.diff: HealthMap and EpiNow exist as standalone surveillance tools that don't talk to the HBYS where the data is born. We're building the first clinic-level sentinel network where outbreak detection is a built-in feature, not a separate service.

vision.layers_title: Five capabilities, three layers of impact.
vision.layer1_body: CoPilot Triage, Whisper Notes, and Photo-In compound to give a single clinician the leverage of a small team. The visit gets faster, safer, and better-documented at the same time — without adding a single hour of training.
vision.layer2_body: Telegram, WhatsApp, and SMS turn the clinic from "come back next week" to "we'll let you know when your lab is ready." Continuity stops being a phone call a tired nurse forgets to make.
vision.layer3_body: Outbreak Watch turns every MediSina-equipped clinic into a sentinel for the region. A disease pattern emerges in the network days before national surveillance picks it up — and the alert reaches the ministry pre-formatted, not pre-buried.
vision.cta_title: Sponsor a capability. Or pilot one.
vision.cta_body: Each of these five is a real engineering investment that can be funded as its own program. Hospital partners can pilot a single capability before committing to the full platform. Donors and foundations can sponsor the build of one capability for a specific region or use case. Talk to us — we'll walk through the engineering plan, the pilot path, and the impact metrics.
